From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: My Refine was taking all my memory and CPU, so I went to Node->Runtime Config and set Parallel-run cap to 2

Body:
My Refine was taking all my memory and CPU, so I went to Node->Runtime Config and set Parallel-run cap to 2.

Can you ask your agent to look at how aggressive refine is being with allocating agents based on your machine specs? I suspect it is being greedy, not assuming room for other expensive processes like large apps running on docker.


[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Buddy Williams

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.
guidance_candidates.name: Intent and architecture
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
guidance_candidates.name: Cohesive code files
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

agent_context.workflow_summary: Refine gives this Goal Agent an isolated worktree and a finalized implementation plan. Implement the current Round and report evidence; a separate agent will review and correct the candidate in Quality, then an independent Governance gate will verify policy and integrate the exact passing commit before human Review. Do not directly advance Goal state, approve, merge, or push.

findings.description: P1 changes budget arithmetic without addressing that available memory and agent RSS are Linux-only and the current RSS sample counts only the managed parent PID, omitting memory-heavy agent descendants such as builds and tests.
findings.recommendation: Extend P1 to define conservative behavior when host memory is unavailable and to account for the full managed agent process tree or process group, with platform and descendant-workload regression tests.

result.summary: Define complete host and agent memory measurement before implementing the conservative concurrency policy.

checklist.description: Revise the host resource governor so automatic admission uses no more than one quarter of detected logical cores and one quarter of currently available memory, keeps at least one slot, reserves at least 2 GiB per agent, aggregates resident memory for each running managed agent root and all of its descendants, falls back to one automatic slot when host memory is unavailable, and rejects incomplete live process-tree samples as evidence for scaling above the conservative reservation.

Keep a positive parallel_run_cap as the authoritative operator override and continue deriving unset node, provider, and target-app limits from the resulting global limit so conservative automatic admission does not weaken deliberate local controls.

Change Node Runtime Config to render an unset parallel-run cap as automatic without displaying or persisting a fixed value of 5, and explain that entering a number overrides the conservative shared-host recommendation.

Add resource-governor regression coverage for quarter-host budgeting, unavailable host memory, low samples constrained by the 2 GiB floor, and aggregate descendant workloads so Linux parent-only RSS and unsupported-platform behavior cannot restore aggressive admission.

Update only the affected Process and browser Settings intent pages to define conservative automatic shared-host concurrency, complete managed-agent workload accounting, and the explicit node-level override.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P1 now defines fail-conservative behavior when host memory or a live process-tree sample is unavailable and measures each managed agent together with all descendants, while P4 adds platform-fallback and descendant-workload regression coverage.

result.summary: Make automatic agent concurrency reserve most CPU and memory for Docker and other expensive host work, count each managed agent's descendant workload, fail conservative when memory cannot be measured, preserve explicit caps such as 2, and make automatic versus manual Runtime Config behavior clear.

governance_precheck.message: The finalized plan can be executed without violating the Constitution, governance rules, or enabled guidance.

checklist.description: Revise the host resource governor to budget at most one quarter of detected logical cores and one quarter of currently available memory for agents, retain a minimum concurrency of one, and use a 2 GiB per-agent floor so an early low RSS sample can only make admission more conservative rather than trigger a launch burst.

Keep a positive parallel_run_cap as the authoritative operator override and continue deriving unset node, provider, and target-app limits from the resulting global limit so conservative automatic admission does not weaken deliberate local controls.

Change Node Runtime Config to represent an unset parallel-run cap as automatic instead of displaying and accidentally persisting a fixed value of 5, and explain that entering a number overrides the shared-host recommendation.
Update the affected Process and browser Settings intent pages to define automatic concurrency as a conservative shared-host default with an explicit node-level escape hatch.

result.summary: Make automatic agent concurrency reserve most host CPU and memory for Docker and other expensive work while preserving an explicit node cap such as 2 and making automatic versus manual behavior clear in Runtime Config.
